personalInfo.name: Kaushal Kumar Agarwal
personalInfo.title: AI/ML Engineer | MCS @ Rice University
personalInfo.summary: Software Engineer with experience across backend, data/ML systems, and cloud platforms. Built scalable APIs, retrieval systems, and serverless data platforms. Strong in Python, Java, C#, AWS, Spark, Docker/Kubernetes, and modern web frameworks.

experience.description:
Leading RAG and agentic AI solutions end-to-end.

Timeline:
- Mid Feb – Early Apr: Researched knowledge-graph RAG using AWS Neptune and Neo4j AuraDB. Built pipelines to enrich JSON metadata for multi-format documents and construct graphs; prototyped natural-language → Cypher translation via LLM prompting/tool-calling to enable complex multi-hop queries.
- Apr – May: Built LLM-powered data cleaning to normalize hierarchical multi-tag columns in batches with guardrails and QC checks, reducing redundancy and improving downstream retrieval quality.
- May – Jul: Implemented a PDF chatbot that returns grounded answers with citations and page-level highlights. Built test/briefing document generation over multi-document sets using Amazon OpenSearch vector DB + Amazon Bedrock LLMs with re-ranking. In parallel, evaluated document/face detection (OpenCV, PaddleOCR, EasyOCR) to identify driver’s licenses and tuned extraction prompts.
- Late Jul – Aug: Productionized the chatbot and document generators with AWS Lambda and Step Functions; restricted actions strictly to one selected manual, added monitoring/alerts, and optimized latency/cost.

Agentic patterns: Tool-augmented LLMs orchestrating retrieval, re-ranking, citation extraction, page locator, OCR, and graph-query tools under policy constraints; evaluation harnesses and observability for reliability.
Managed grading and office hours for OOP, Computer Security, Software Engineering Methodology, and Software Construction; improved assignment scores by ~10% via targeted support.
Engineered C#/.NET backend APIs aggregating data from ~2,000 GitLab repos. Delivered role-based dashboards enabling leadership insights on MR review efficiency and developer performance.

Promoted to Software Engineer II within a year. Owned design and implementation of serverless APIs in Python on AWS Lambda to deliver new features and bug fixes. Managed Bitbucket CI/CD pipelines and Amorphic release cycles (dev → qa → staging → master), including packaging release artifacts to S3 and deploying via CMP. Provided on-call support for developers/customers, proactively shipped features, and patched production issues.

A) Dataset Metrics Collection (New Feature)
- Requirement: For each dataset (with many files, mutable over time), collect daily time series metrics (TotalFileSize, NumberOfFiles).
- Challenges: Full file scans are slow for Lambda; migrated to AWS Glue job, scheduled via CloudWatch Events (midnight), with backfill synchronization from dataset creation to present.
- Output: Time-series visualization to spot anomalies; automated email notifications to dataset owners.

B) Dataset Lifecycle Mechanism (Customer Demand)
- Requirement: Configure file expiration after X days and tier migration to specific S3 storage classes after Y days.
- Challenges: High-risk operation; used AWS Step Functions to orchestrate create/modify lifecycle rules at S3 prefix level with rollback on failures; robust error handling and notifications.
- Output: Increased customer trust and retention; contributed to revenue growth. Future: Glacier restore workflows.

C) AWS EKS Upgrade (1.21 → 1.24)
- Context: Cluster running Apache Superset and AWS Load Balancer Controller.
- Challenges: Reverse-engineered provisioning/install steps; extensive troubleshooting and compatibility validation.
- Result: Technically validated upgrade path; postponed due to limited customer engagement.

D) Error Code Standardization
- Goal: Unify exception message structure across services.
- Challenges: Designing a common error code template and consolidating multi-source error messages.
- Result: Improved code quality and operability.

E) Release Cycle Process
- Flow: dev → qa(testing) → staging(testing) → master(testing).
- Artifacts: Versioned release bundles in S3; used by CMP to deploy to customer environments.

F) Customer Environment Ops
- Patching Lambda processes; salt key rotation for PAT security.

G) Initiatives
- Piloted AWS CodeGuru (Code Reviewer, Lambda Profiler, Code Security).
- Reduced PyLint stage time by ~50% in Bitbucket pipelines.
- Researched observability (logs, traces, metrics) via AWS Grafana and CloudWatch Logs Insights.

Designed and developed a Scala-based Spark metrics framework to capture rich event data and accelerate performance analysis; achieved ~10% speedup on TPC-DS benchmarks. Optimized regression runs using PyTest with multiprocessing and Jenkins by parallelizing across ephemeral child accounts spawned from a parent account. Addressed per-account configuration reinitialization and teardown for isolation and reproducibility, reducing regression time roughly by a factor of N (number of cores).

J.A.R.V.I.S.S.: Contributed to a microservice-based multi-cloud security orchestration platform offering unified, cloud-agnostic terminology, tag-based policy enforcement resilient to cloud migrations, and cloud graph visualization to inspect live connections. Integrated AWS and GCP (extensible to Azure/Kubernetes/private clouds). Implemented components using Terraform, HashiCorp Vault, Flask, and MongoDB, leading to ~15% reduction in operational costs.

Developed decentralized applications using Flo-Blockchain: FloSecretSharingApp - Decentralized app to store secrets on blockchain using encryption with Shamir’s algorithm. FloAppStore - Python-based GUI app store (Tkinter), with all app metadata stored on blockchain. FloWhatsapp - Peer-to-peer web chat app using JavaScript, IndexedDB, Mongoose Client (C++), and blockchain.

projects.name: Chest X-ray Medical Report Generation
projects.description: Implemented transfer learning and encoder-decoder architectures for automated report generation; achieved BLEU ~0.322, improving baselines by ~30%.

projects.name: TV Series Dubber
projects.description: Python-based pipeline to dub TV series episodes using subtitles, TTS (Google or Amazon Polly), FFmpeg, and the open-source Vocal-Remover project. Multithreaded workflow: 1) Convert subtitles to speech and generate MP3; 2) Separate voice/background audio; 3) Recompose video with background track and generated speech.
